summary: Authenticated SIEM ingest with per-event identity enrichment and signed delivery manifest
description:
Issue summary:
Customer requests a certified SIEM ingest that includes per-event authenticated envelopes, field-level identity enrichment (map Redwood user_id -> customer org_user_id), and a signed delivery manifest for every hourly batch.

Impact:
NorthBridge Finance needs this for their regulatory audit next month (financial services). Without a cryptographically verifiable delivery manifest and identity mapping, their compliance team will not accept Redwood as an approved data source. This is blocking their production rollout.

Requested deliverables:
- Real-time or near-real-time HEC/HTTPS endpoint with mutual TLS and per-message signature (HMAC-SHA256) or detachable signature header.
- Per-event identity enrichment: include "org_user_id" and "tenant_role" in the exported envelope, sourced from the request context when available.
- Hourly signed manifest (JSON or NDJSON) listing batch start/end, event count, cumulative HMAC, and per-file checksum. Manifest must be signed with Redwood's export keystore and include key-id and signature algorithm.
- Retention assertions and proof of non-modification for the last 90 days (RPO/RTO statements, sample signed snapshots).

Customer-provided constraints:
- All artifacts must meet NorthBridge legal's evidence ingestion checklist (they supplied a questionnaire).
- Destination SIEM is Splunk HEC (on-prem) behind an MTLS proxy.

Notes: customer prefers push-based delivery; if push is not possible, they accept scheduled S3 drops with signed manifests and presigned URL rotation.

investigation_notes: Checked current audit-export pipeline: supports bulk S3 dumps with per-file checksum, but no per-event detachable signature header; HMAC computed at batch level only.

Serving runtime currently captures request.user_id and request.token metadata; a deterministic join to customer org mapping can be performed if we expose a lookup table or allow customer to supply mapping file during onboarding.
Keystore: Redwood KMS supports asymmetric signing (ECDSA/PSS) and HMAC keys. Need to document rotation window and publication of public keys for NorthBridge verification.
Network: MTLS fronting to customer on-prem is supported by our webhook delivery stack; confirm cipher suites and SNI expectations with customer.

Risk: per-event signing adds CPU overhead. Consider signing manifest aggregates instead of each event; customer explicitly requested per-event identity assertion inside envelope with HMAC header on request — propose hybrid: include org_user_id in envelope, HMAC per-batch and per-file checksums, with optional per-event signature in high-compliance tier.
Linked internal ticket INT-2023 created to track mapping implementation; security review ticket INT-2047 opened for KMS signing policy.
Relevant dashboards: Datadog export-latency-playback, Kibana: export-errors-prod-us-east. Shared links in Confluence.
resolution_notes:
Planned deliverables and interim workaround:
- Short term (within 3 business days): produce weekly signed CSV bundles with manifest and provide sample signed snapshot for legal acceptance. Customer accepted as interim.
- Mid term (2-3 weeks): implement mapping join in export pipeline (INT-2023) to include org_user_id and tenant_role inside event envelope. Produce hourly manifests signed with Redwood KMS key; publish key-id and proof of rotation policy.
- Long term: evaluate per-event detachable signatures as opt-in for enterprise compliance customers; document CPU/cost implications and provide pricing add-on.

Follow-ups:
- Security to complete INT-2047 for KMS signing policy and key publication.
- SRE to deliver mapping implementation and run performance tests.
- Support to prepare evidence bundle and confirm acceptance with NorthBridge legal.

Status: awaiting security review (INT-2047) and mapping implementation (INT-2023). Interim weekly signed delivery scheduled and confirmed with customer.
